story.head: Penalties could cost the Blue Jackets
paras: The Stars won the teams’ first meeting this season, 3-1 in Dallas on Saturday. The Stars come in at 8-5-1, the Blue Jackets at 5-7-0. Going in, the Stars are fourth in the Central (tied for 13th in the NHL) and the Jackets last in the Metropolitan (tied for 29th).

The Stars’ record (.607) is about what their chances are worth. The Blue Jackets have played better than their record (.417) says: their chances are worth about .482, and their finishing has held them back.

The Stars block more shots than anyone (1st) and have a dangerous power play (2nd). Dallas has allowed 2.14 goals a game, the fewest in the league. The Blue Jackets get their defensemen shooting (5th) and keep things calm after the whistle (5th lowest). They also have a leaky penalty kill (30th), so the Stars’ power play (2nd) could do real damage when they’re shorthanded. Columbus has scored 2.33 goals a game, the fourth fewest in the league. Both teams play slow, low-event hockey, especially the Stars (lowest), so expect a tight one.

Mikko Rantanen (7 G / 10 A / 17 P in 14 GP) leads the Stars in scoring, and Jason Robertson (5 G / 9 A / 14 P in 14 GP) is next in line. For the Blue Jackets, Kent Johnson (7 G / 5 A / 12 P in 12 GP) leads the way in scoring, with seven points in his last five games. Zach Werenski (0 G / 10 A / 10 P in 12 GP) isn’t far behind.

Jake Oettinger (7-3-1 / .922 SV% in 11 GS) has been outstanding for Dallas and will likely start. Columbus has two options in net: Jet Greaves (2-5-0 / .882 SV% in 7 GS) and Cam Talbot (3-2-0 / .893 SV% in 5 GS). They have split the last ten starts, and Greaves got the last one on Saturday. It’s anyone’s guess who gets the net.
At home, Rick Bowness likes to send Sillinger, Monahan and Garland out against opponents’ third lines, so watch for them against Perron, Hyry and Benn.
